subject: MSstats Comparison Behavior (Multiple Comparison in one run)

messages.author: 5cb4863e55f8ea3c
messages.subject: MSstats Comparison Behavior (Multiple Comparison in one run)
parts:
MSstats team,
Our lab has been noticing some strange behavior in the MSstats comparison outputs which seems to be independent of results from normalization through protein summarization.
Basically, the Log2FC and p-values for some proteins don't match up with what we would expect from seeing the raw data (chromatograms and intensity values), and interestingly don't seem to agree with the MSstats modeled run level protein abundance values.

Please take a look at two brief examples that we noticed recently.  I have tried to include as many of the relevant files as possible, but I will be happy to provide you with whatever additional information you need.  I have included in this post the Rscript used to run the analysis, and can provide a link to an Rdata file containing all of the raw inputs and outputs from our analysis...

Example 1:
Protein TBC13 (sp|Q9NVG8|TBC13_HUMAN).  This protein has intensity data for 3 of 4 conditions, but only one peptide.  The control the for final comparison was the mCherry-BID condition.  Below is the full TMP_result$ProcessedData table (filtered for TBC13):



As I hope you'll be able to see, the last condition (SLC25A46-L341P-BID) has "1" values for intensity/"0" vakyes fir abundance, with TRUE for censored.  These peaks were rejected at q<=.01 by our mProphet peak picking model during Skyline analysis.
You may also notice that the "mCherry-BID" condition has much higher intensities for this peptide/protein than the other conditions.

So, the next question I had was how the $RunLevelData looked across runs:


We can see here that the SLC25A46-L341P-BID condition is missing from the RunlevelData protein abundance.


We can see from the ComparisonResult that all three conditions appear to be "Inf" enriched over the control, which was mCherry-BID.  This does not make sense to me given the previous data, and appears to disagree with the previous outputs/inputs.



Example 2:

Protein S2546 (sp|Q96AG3|S2546_HUMAN).  This protein has many peptides, and there is at least one peptide with intensity data from all conditions.  Therefore, this example may illustrate a different problem than the previous protein.
I will start at the RunLevelData output.  Here we can see that all four conditions (and all eight runs) have summarized intensities.


You can see here that the log(intensity) values for the condition SLAC25A46-BID are much higher than any other condition.  This is supported by direct interrogation of the extracted ion chromatograms.  But, the comparisonResult does not seem to agree with what we would expect from the RunLevelData:



With mCherry-BID as the control in this, as well, I am deeply confused by the directionality of the Log2FC values.

All of the above data was generated using MSstats 3.7.3.

Attached to this post is the R script which was run to generate the analysis examined above.  Please let me know if we can help in any way with troubleshooting or providing additional information, such as the aforementioned Rdata image/environment.

Thanks so much for the help.  Please let me know if I have done something incorrectly/strangely.

Best,
William

messages.author: df9ba0266a9a081f
messages.subject: Re: MSstats Comparison Behavior (Multiple Comparison in one run)
parts:
Dear William,

I attach the updated R script with some comments. Here is the summary.

1. comparison matrix seems different than you explain. As I understand, you want to compare other 3 condition with 'mCherry-BID'. Then comparison matrix is not as you described. Please check R script. After changing comparison matrix, it seems to work well.
2. I assume that the dataset is for DDA and the output from Skyline. Then, please use 'SkylinetoMSstatsFormat' function before 'dataProcess' function, which will handle truncated peaks, monoisotopic peaks and so on. (msstats manual, section 4.2.2, p 31)
3. For skyline output, censoredInt='0', because NAs in Skyline are random.

Hope to help.
- Meena
